title: Responsive Images
definition: Images that scale nicely to fit any browser size. In modern web development, an image should never overflow its container or stretch out of proportion.
simpleExplanation: If you put a 2000px wide 4K image on a 400px wide iPhone, the image will physically stick out of the phone's screen and cause a horizontal scrollbar. You fix this by telling the image: 'Never be wider than your parent container'.
realWorldExample: The holy grail rule of responsive images: `img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }`.

basic: What CSS property prevents an image from overflowing its container?

answers.question: max-width vs width?
answers.answer: If you have a tiny 50px icon inside a giant 1000px container, `width: 100%` will forcefully stretch the icon to 1000px, making it incredibly blurry. `max-width: 100%` means 'Shrink if you have to, but never grow larger than your original file size'.

codeExample: Resize your browser! The red container shrinks, and the massive image automatically scales down with it, never breaking out of the red box.
